issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for class Animal: the UML in problem_statement.md (line 29) declares a two-parameter constructor 'Animal(String, int)' (name and age), but the example usage in the template (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java, lines 9-11) and the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java, line 6) provide and expect a single-parameter constructor 'Animal(String)'. This inconsistency leaves students unsure whether to implement a two-argument constructor including an int age (and update all concrete subclasses and example code) or a single-argument constructor as used in the template and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor specification consistent across artifacts. Option A (preferred for current template/solution): update the UML in problem_statement.md to declare 'Animal(String)' and remove the age attribute from the UML. Option B: update the template and solution to add a private int age field and change constructors to 'public Animal(String name, int age)', then update all concrete subclass constructors (Seal, Pig, Goat) and the example usages in Main.java and tests accordingly.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch for class Animal: the UML in problem_statement.md (line 28) declares an 'age: int' attribute on Animal, but the solution implementation (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Animal.java, line 4) and the template/example usage (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Main.java, lines 9-11) do not define or use any 'age' field. Students will be unclear whether they must add an 'age' attribute (with its getter/setter) to Animal or omit it.
issues.suggestedFix: Resolve the attribute discrepancy by either removing the 'age' attribute from the UML in problem_statement.md (if age is not required for the exercises) or by adding a private int age field to the Animal class in the template and solution, providing appropriate constructor parameters, getters/setters, and updating all subclass constructors and example usages in Main.java and tests to supply an age value.
